top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a single, bounded invention: a magic-wavelength lattice cancels the trapping Stark shift while Lamb-Dicke confinement suppresses Doppler and recoil effects, so many neutral atoms can be interrogated on a narrow optical transition. It is mature, reproduced and surpassed by independent laboratories, and the Katori (concept) and Ye (record accuracy and coherence) allocation is natural. A citation naming the lattice clock and magic-wavelength trapping separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. The topological insulator prize (P002) is scientifically first-rank but carries an unresolved attribution gap (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Zhang deceased) and is only supported by one member, so it ranks second; no award is last.
recusal_note: none apparent for P001 or P002 from profile; my documented superconducting-circuit and WACQT/Chalmers links (Delsing, Wilson, 2025 prize hosts) bear only on B058, which is not in this slate
